newsitem.title: ITALY: Bad luck of the draw robs Italy lottery winner.
newsitem.headline: Bad luck of the draw robs Italy lottery winner.

text.p: The happy owner of a ticket picked as the winner of one of the top prizes in Italy's biggest lottery had a rude shock on Tuesday when the state games committee declared the ticket invalid because of a technical problem.
Ticket number U 527243, sold in the eastern town of Jesi, was drawn live on television on Monday night to win fifth prize, two billion lire ($1.3 million), in the New Year Lottery draw.

But a blockage caused six instead of 10 balls to drop in one of the machines from which the winning number was drawn. The General Games Committee, after a 45-minute meeting, decided that the win was void and the ticket should be cancelled.
It was replaced with ticket I 771131, the first drawn after the original top six winners had been selected. Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said he was opening an inquiry into the foul-up.
The lottery's top prize was seven billion lire.
Italians greeted the news with horror. Psychologists warned that the "virtual winner" could turn aggressive or, if an elderly person, could have a heart attack or even die of shock.
Lawyers said he or she may be able to appeal and consumers' association Codacons called on Visco to authorise a re-draw.
Italy has had problems with its lottery before.

Last May, the Finance Ministry admitted that a disproportionate number of winning tickets in the instant "scratch 'n win" lottery had been sent to the northern province of Bergamo, where punters won 10 billlion lire in three days. ($1=1,535 lire)
